_comment: RETIRING — EMPTY OF CONTENT since 2026-10-01 (bean `j7ql`, epic `7x5n`, issue #1770). Owner ruling 2026-10-01: agent-skills becomes a subgraph of cat-harness, DISSOLVED into cat-harness's concern groups rather than nested as a whole directory. Its 14 library documents are in `cat-harness/library/<slug>/` (summaries still HELD, per entry, via `heldEntries`), its voices in `cat-harness/skills/voices/` (declared from within by `cat-harness/skills/skills.json`), and its image verdicts merged into `cat-harness/library/image-verdicts.json` with their attribution kept per document. This declaration and the directory it sits in are kept, not deleted: retiring a declared instance is the OWNER's call (`deletion-requires-confirmation`), and what would go is listed on bean `j7ql`. Until then it declares no directory — declare only what exists (bean `dh4f`) — and needs only cat-harness, which now holds everything it held; it no longer needs folio-assistant-core. The previous comment, kept for the record: THE AGENT-SKILL LITERATURE, staged as a top-level directory ahead of becoming its own repository — the same arrangement as who-iris/, who-style-guide/, folio-assistant-sci/ and folio-assistant-core/. It holds the corpus of published guidance on authoring and operating agent skills, and the voices read out of it. ONE instance rather than the who-iris/who-style-guide pair, and the reason is the corpus: that pair is split because IRIS is a catalogue of a million items from which three were read, so the corpus and the reading have genuinely different scopes. Here the corpus IS the subject — every document in it exists to be read into these voices — so splitting would put two directories in two repositories with a one-to-one relation between them. Same shape as folio-assistant-sci, which holds `library/milnorlink` and is where the `milnor` voice is going. THIS IS NOT PLATFORM CONTENT: `AGENTS.md` opens by saying folio-assistant is the platform and not the content, and vendor documentation about skill authoring is somebody else's writing, so it does not go in cat-harness even though it is ABOUT the harness's own subject.
